_common: Seamless tileable texture. Flat orthographic scan of the material, camera perfectly perpendicular to the surface, the material fills the entire square frame edge to edge. Perfectly even soft diffuse lighting, no perspective, no cast shadows, no vignetting, no specular highlights, no objects, no people, no text, no logo, no watermark, no border, no frame. Photorealistic, high detail, true-to-life colors. Mood: The Backrooms liminal space, old, yellowed, slightly dirty, signs of long use but completely empty.
wallpaper_l0: Old mono-yellow office wallpaper from The Backrooms Level 0. Muted mustard yellow paper covered with a faint low-contrast regular pattern: thin vertical pinstripes and small repeating diamond motifs in a slightly darker yellow, arranged on a strict regular grid (exactly 6 diamond columns across and 6 rows down). Fine paper grain, subtle aged discoloration, a few very faint pale brown water stains. The overall color must stay clearly yellow.
carpet_l0: Damp, worn, Berber-style tight loop-pile commercial carpet, brownish beige color, coarse synthetic fibers, irregular darker moist patches and faint mildew discoloration, grimy and old. Viewed straight from above.
carpet_light: Short loop-pile carpet in a soft light pastel yellow (butter yellow), fine even fibers, clean but slightly aged, very subtle color variation. Viewed straight from above. The color must be clearly light yellow, not white and not beige.
ceiling_tile: Surface of an old mineral-fiber acoustic drop-ceiling tile: off-white slightly yellowed material with the typical random fissured pinhole and worm-track pattern, a few very faint pale yellow-brown water stains. Close-up of the tile surface only, no grid bars, no seams, no edges.
light_panel: One square recessed fluorescent ceiling light troffer seen straight on from directly below, switched on and glowing bright white. A parabolic aluminum louver grid (egg-crate pattern, 4 by 4 square cells) covers the glowing tubes, a thin white metal frame runs around the outer edge. The panel fills the entire frame exactly, symmetric, even exposure, no surrounding ceiling.
concrete: Plain grey poured concrete surface, slightly rough with small pores and pits, faint darker stains and scuffs, aged and dusty. Viewed straight on.
concrete_wet: Damp dark grey concrete floor, irregular wet patches that darken the surface, shallow dried puddle marks, grime, small pores and pits, aged. Matte wet look without reflections. Viewed straight from above.
l3_brick_brown: Old dusty brown brick wall from an industrial power station corridor. Weathered reddish-brown clay bricks with visible mortar lines, thick even layer of grey dust and grime on the surface, a few dark patina stains as if copper pipes once ran across it. Viewed straight on.
l3_tile_gray: Worn grey ceramic floor tile, dust-covered, small square tiles in a regular grid with thin darker grout lines, matte and slightly scuffed, faint dark grime patches. Viewed straight from above.
l5_wallpaper_hotel: Opulent 1930s hotel wallpaper from The Backrooms Level 5. Deep red mahogany background color covered with an ornate low-contrast regular pattern of thin gold-colored fleur-de-lis and filigree motifs, arranged on a strict regular grid (exactly 5 motif columns across and 5 rows down). Fine paper grain, subtle aged discoloration, a couple of faint pale water stains. The overall color must stay clearly deep red/mahogany with gold accents, elegant vintage hotel decor.
l5_carpet_hotel: Exotic richly patterned antique hotel carpet, red and gold tones, dense cut-pile commercial carpet with an ornate interlocking damask-style swirl pattern, worn but well cared for, faint dust. Viewed straight from above. The overall color must stay clearly warm red and gold, opulent 1930s hotel style.
l11_apartment_windows: Flat elevation view of a wide plain grey concrete apartment building facade from The Backrooms Level 11, an endless ordinary city. Small square windows arranged in a strict regular grid (exactly 6 columns across and 6 rows down), most window panes dark and blank like dim black mirrors, a few scattered panes lit with a warm dull yellow glow. Plain unremarkable stucco-like grey wall between windows, faint weathering, subtle grime streaks below window sills, no balconies, no text, no signage.
l8_cave_rock: Natural wild cave rock surface from a limestone cavern system, unworked by any tool. Rough grey-brown stone with fine mineral veining, small embedded crystal flecks, subtle damp water-seepage staining running down in irregular streaks, uneven pitted and pocked surface typical of stalactite and stalagmite rock. No bricks, no mortar lines, no cut edges, entirely organic natural stone.
l10_soil: Tilled farmland topsoil from an open wheat field, dark brown loamy dirt with small crumbly clumps, a few scattered dry straw stalks and small pebbles pressed into the surface, faint darker moist patches, uneven natural texture typical of ploughed soil. Viewed straight from above.
l13_wall_plaster: Dull off-white and beige painted plaster wall from a mundane mid-20th-century apartment building hallway. Slightly uneven hand-painted plaster surface with faint trowel texture, a few small hairline cracks, scattered scuff marks and dull discoloration at hand height, one subtle patch where a different slightly darker beige paint was used to cover a stain. Flat, unremarkable, dreary institutional apartment corridor paint job. Viewed straight on.
l13_floor_linoleum: Worn beige-brown linoleum tile flooring from a dated apartment hallway, faint mottled marbling pattern typical of cheap laminate/linoleum sheet flooring, dulled matte finish with scuff trails and a few small scratches, faint grime built up along seams. Viewed straight from above.
l16_moss_ground: Dense tropical rainforest forest floor ground cover. Rich dark brown damp soil partly covered with fallen green leaves, small ferns and patches of thick moss, thin tangled roots breaking the surface, faint low ground mist clinging between the leaves. Viewed straight from above.
l16_ice_surface: Frozen glacial ice sheet surface, pale blue-white color, highly reflective and glassy, subtle fine cracks and stress fractures running through the ice in irregular branching lines, a light dusting of fresh snow in a few patches, cold arctic tundra look. Viewed straight from above.
l14_wall_hospital: Painted plaster interior wall from an abandoned hospital corridor. Pale beige and dusty peach color, small chipped patches revealing an off-white undercoat beneath, faint brownish water stains trailing down from hairline cracks, light scuff marks near the bottom edge, old and worn, no fixtures, no baseboards, no text.
l15_pipe_glyph: Close-up macro photo of a section of white painted steel pipe surface, seamless tileable, camera perpendicular. Smooth glossy white enamel paint over metal, faint scattered small rust freckles, a few light scuff marks and paint chips. Faintly embossed pale gray-white repeating pattern resembling a stylized vine or ivy tendril motif engraved into the metal, very low contrast, barely visible against the white paint, mysterious unreadable symbol, no text, no logo.
l14_floor_hospital: Light grey vinyl composition hospital floor tile, matte low-sheen finish, faint reddish-brown directional stripe markings and scattered dark scuff marks, small embedded dark flecks, aged and slightly dulled. Viewed straight from above.
l19_floor_attic: Old creaky attic floorboards, narrow warped wooden planks laid parallel, worn grey-brown wood grain with visible growth rings, dust and grime built up in the gaps between boards, a few small dark stains and scattered splinters, dry aged timber. Viewed straight from above.
l19_wall_attic: Old vertical wooden plank wall from a cluttered attic, dark aged brown wood grain with visible knots, narrow gaps between boards showing slight warping, a few damp mildew stains and scattered small water marks, dusty and neglected, no fixtures, no baseboards, no text.
l18_wall_nursery: Painted plaster nursery wall from a preschool or daycare classroom in The Backrooms. Soft muted mint-green paint above, a horizontal band near the bottom third of the wall showing a simple repeating hand-painted mural: a red square, a yellow star and a blue circle evenly spaced in a strict regular row (exactly 4 repeats across), faded crayon-like colors, plain smooth plaster elsewhere with a couple of small scuffs and light scratches at child height, no fixtures, no baseboards, no text.
lrun_wall_scratched: Old dusty plaster or concrete wall surface from a long-abandoned corridor. Pale dusty grey-beige color with a heavy even layer of settled dust, several sets of deep parallel claw-like scratch gouges raked diagonally across the surface exposing a slightly lighter substrate beneath, subtle faded water staining and a few hairline cracks, worn and forgotten. No bricks, no tiles, no fixtures, no baseboards.
